Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a renowned truth-seeker and detective, traveling under the alias Gagan Mitra in this case.

Ajit.description: The narrator and close companion of Byomkesh, chronicling the events of the investigation.

Phanish.description: A young, gentle man, son of Manish Babu, recently married to Indira and entangled in a murder case.

Indira.description: Phanish's young, shy wife, concerned for her husband's safety and the daughter-in-law of the household.

Manish Babu.description: Owner of a coal mine and father of Phanish, a man of traditional values and influence.

Gobinda Halder.description: Owner of a neighboring coal mine, described as cunning and intimidating, brother of Aravinda.

Gagan Mitra.description: Alias used by Byomkesh during the investigation.

Sujit Bandyopadhyay.description: Alias used by Ajit during the investigation.

Surapati Ghatak.description: The caretaker and office master of the colliery's main office, known for his experience.

Tarapada Babu.description: The elderly manager of the coal mine, responsible for its operations.

Dr. Jatindra Ghosh.description: The physician at the mine's dispensary and hospital, a contemporary of Byomkesh and Ajit.

Aravinda.description: Gobinda Halder's younger brother and business partner, notorious for his vices and bad reputation.

Mrigendra Moulik.description: Owner of the Uludanga coal mine and a member of the Coal Club gambling group.

Madhumoy Sur.description: Owner of the Dhupipota mine and a member of the Coal Club gambling group.

Pranahari Poddar.description: An elderly, shrewd moneylender and skilled card player, whose murder is central to the case.

Mohini.description: Pranahari Poddar's young, attractive maidservant from Orissa, suspected in the murder investigation.

Promod Barat.description: The chief inspector of the city’s main police station, an acquaintance of Byomkesh.

Bikash.description: A clever young man known to Byomkesh, summoned to work as a compounder at the colliery dispensary.

Calcutta.description: A major Indian city, now known as Kolkata, referenced as the origin of some characters.

swadeshi.description: A movement and set of customs promoting Indian-made goods and traditional practices.

Uludanga.description: A locality referenced as the site of a coal mine and the road where Pranahari Poddar lived.

Dhupipota.description: A locality referenced as the site of a coal mine owned by Madhumoy Sur.

Shimulia.description: A locality referenced as the site of a coal mine owned by the Halder brothers.

Cuttack.description: A city in the state of Orissa (now Odisha), where Pranahari Poddar previously lived.

Orissa.description: An Indian state (now called Odisha), the home state of Mohini and Pranahari Poddar's previous residence.

Coal Club.description: An exclusive club in the city for elite members, where gambling and card games take place.

Uludanga Khoni Road.description: A road leading to Uludanga, where Pranahari Poddar's house is located.

Fuljhuri Colliery.description: The coal mine owned by Manish Babu and central to the story's events.

Golap Colony.description: A previous case referenced, where Byomkesh and Promod Barat became acquainted.

Doropani.description: A location referenced as a base for Byomkesh's intelligence gathering.

Yale lock.description: A brand of lock, noted for its security, used on Pranahari Poddar's door.

babu.description: A term of respect for a man, especially in Bengal.

Mahashay.description: A respectful Bengali honorific, similar to 'sir' or 'gentleman.'

daroga-babu.description: A respectful term for a police inspector or sub-inspector.

dhuti.description: A traditional Indian men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

panjabi.description: A knee-length tunic worn by men, especially in Bengal.

Pharasdanga dhuti.description: A specific style or quality of dhuti, indicating a fine or formal garment.

bazar.description: Market; refers to a commercial area or marketplace.

para.description: A neighborhood or locality, especially in Bengali contexts.

baithak-khana.description: A drawing-room or sitting room in a Bengali household.

compounder.description: A medical assistant who prepares and dispenses medicines, often in a dispensary or clinic.

PM report.description: Post-mortem report; the official autopsy findings.
